title: The Big 5 of Inequality
subtitle: What a new wave could mean for affordability in America

images.caption: Renters earning under $30,000 had a record-low $210 a month left after rent and utilities in 2024, down from $410 in 2019. Source: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies
ACA Marketplace enrollment fell 13% in 2026, from 22.1 million to 19.2 million people, after the enhanced subsidies expired. Source: KFF
Thirteen-year-olds’ average math score rose 21 points from 1978 to 2012, then lost 15 of them by 2025. Source: NCES, NAEP Long-Term Trend
92% of children born in 1940 grew up to out-earn their parents. For children born in 1984, it was a coin flip at 50%. Source: Opportunity Insights
Recent college graduates have had higher unemployment than the average worker since 2019, the longest such stretch in data going back to 1990. Source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
